summary_for_children: Ar-Ra'd shows rivers, gardens, lightning and thunder as signs of Allah, and compares truth to water that stays and falsehood to foam that goes away.
environment_concept: The valley of thunder: rivers running between mountains (13:3), neighbouring plots growing different fruits from one water (13:4), a ridge and a rocky hall under thunder clouds (13:12-13) and a pool where foam drifts away (13:17).
architecture_and_scenery: River valley between mountains, terraced neighbouring plots, palm groves, storm clouds.

unique_world.visual_theme: A high green valley under big skies with a rock overhang, three hollows of different sizes and a field below each

primary_mechanic.text: A storm comes on its own; shelter under the rock overhang while lightning flashes, watch each valley fill by its own size, then cast the foam off the water so what benefits stays and waters the fields (13:17).

secondary_activities: lightning safety: wait out the storm in shelter
neighbouring fields watered with one water (13:4)
unique_world.narrative_structure: Lookout reading, then the storm and the valleys, then the fields, then quiet under the overhang
world_assets: three valley pools that rise with the rain
environment_behaviour: clouds gather and darken, rain falls and lightning flashes the sky
valley water rises by each valley's size
foam slowly breaks up on its own and is cast off faster by hand
ground birds lift off in the storm
unique_world.learning_objective: See the parable of 13:17: what looks big on top does not last, what benefits people remains

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Voice of Thunder
story_library.children_narration: Have you ever watched the sky become dark before a storm? Have you heard the powerful sound of thunder? Surah Ar-Ra'd invites us to notice the wonders around us: clouds, rain, mountains, rivers, and growing plants. Rain falls from the sky, and valleys carry water according to their capacity. The Quran also gives the example of foam floating on water. The foam disappears, while what benefits people remains. This teaches us to think about the difference between what is true and lasting and what quickly disappears.

world_idea.title: The Storm Valley
world_idea.description: Explore a changing mountain environment, watch rainwater flow through valleys, experiment with safe water channels, and observe the difference between foam and water. This is a nature-based reflection adventure, not a historical event.
